records.name: Friends of the Cresheim Trail
records.summary: A volunteer nonprofit that builds and looks after trails linking Wissahickon Valley Park with Fort Washington State Park. Its current project is a rail trail on old railroad land.
records.what_you_do: Join cleanups and trail workdays, help at fundraisers and booths, or support the group with a membership donation.

schedule.text: Cleanups and volunteer workdays on weekends, mostly in spring and fall, plus a yearly fundraiser. The latest dated items were a May 16, 2026 cleanup and a May 29, 2026 fundraiser.

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteer workdays. Membership has a suggested donation of about $50. Fundraiser tickets start at $40 on a sliding scale.

first_step.how: Register for the next volunteer workday using the link posted with that event, or email info@cresheimtrail.org with questions
first_step.basis: Workdays are open to volunteers and the group says how to register for each one, though its site does not describe a general sign up process.

records.notes: The seed had no address; the location is the group's usual start point at Mermaid Park, from the group's site. A cleanup recap on the site is undated. Older posts mention fall cleanups and a September workday with no years shown. Instagram and Facebook are linked but were not read. The June 21, 2026 outing had no details posted yet.

records.name: Friends of FDR Park
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports South Philadelphia's largest park. It backs park programs and local wildlife and works toward a long-term park plan.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member (dues start at $25), volunteer on park work, or donate. The group says donations go to the park.

schedule.text: Events are posted on the group's public calendar, but the pages we read showed no dated events. The park is open every day, with longer hours from April to October.

cost.text: Membership dues start at $25. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Join as a member through the membership link on the group's site, or email info@fdrpark.org to ask how to volunteer
first_step.basis: Membership is open to the public and the site gives a clear way to join, but its volunteer steps are not described on the pages we read.

records.notes: The site works and lists contacts and a membership link, but the pages read show no dated events or news. Status is probably_active under the rule for working sites with no dates. records.name: Friends of Fitler Square Park
records.summary: The group that supports Fitler Square Park, a small park on Pine Street between 23rd and 24th Streets. It runs a summer concert series and a yearly fall fundraiser, and it recruits volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Attend the summer concerts and the fall fundraiser, volunteer on park work, or join a committee. Donations and bench adoptions support the park.

schedule.text: A summer concert series in the park, plus a fall fundraiser. The latest dated events were a July 10, 2026 concert, an August 7, 2026 concert, and a September 18, 2026 fundraiser. No upcoming events were listed at this check.

cost.text: Concert and fundraiser prices are not on the pages we read. The fundraiser sells tickets online.

first_step.how: Come to a summer concert in the park, then use the Volunteer page on the group's site or email friendsoffitlersquarepark@gmail.com to ask how to help
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public, and the site lists volunteer, committee and board pages, though the steps for joining are not spelled out.

records.notes: Dates come from the group's events page: July 10, August 7 and September 18, 2026. The September fundraiser marked the park's 130th anniversary and the fountain's 50th. The site listed no upcoming events for October 2026 at this check. Facebook and Instagram are linked and not read.

records.name: Garden Court Community Association
records.summary: A registered community association for the Garden Court neighborhood in West Philadelphia, active since the mid-1950s on neighborhood problems, housing and local gardens. Its news includes park cleanups, a school garden donation, and plant and vegetable giveaways.
records.what_you_do: Join or renew membership through the site, use the Get Involved page to find a way to help, or come to the annual meeting and neighborhood events.

schedule.text: The site lists an annual meeting on a Saturday in June, 1:30 to 3:30 pm, without a year. Other events are posted on the site.

cost.text: The membership amount is not shown on the page we read.

first_step.how: Use the Join or Renew link on the group's site, or email info@gardencourtca.org to ask about the next meeting or cleanup
first_step.basis: The site has a public way to join and a Get Involved page, but it does not describe steps for volunteering.

records.notes: The City list calls this Friends of Garden Court, at the park's address. The website belongs to Garden Court Community Association, which describes itself as a neighborhood association covering 45th to 52nd Streets and Locust to Cedar Avenue. Treated here as the same group; please confirm. The news items on the site are undated, so status is probably_active under the rule for working sites with no dates. The annual meeting date has no year, so it was not used for status. The published mailing address (a P.O. box) was not recorded as a visitor location.
